text:
matt: Heads up — canary p99 doubled after last release (model-gpt-small on canary hosts). Noticing this in eu-west and us-west.

ci-bot: deploy canary finished (sha: abcdef1234). Perf smoke job: perf/smoke/canary triggered.

alex: confirming on dashboards — p50 steady, p99 ~2x. CPU usage on runtime nodes is up, GPU utilization normal.

priya: did we touch kernel selection or batching defaults in that rollout? I remember a tiny PR around selector heuristics.

matt: yep, PR 7a1b2c3 changed prioritization in kernel_selector and also reduced batching_window_ms from 12 -> 6 (to lower latency for small requests). There was also a kv-cache eviction tweak (commit f0e1d2).

sam: can someone bisect? I can run git bisect if we have a deterministic perf harness. Need steps to reproduce locally.

jen: CI smoke (nightly) shows same regression in the Linux perf job: bench/runtime/smoke p99 jumped. Attaching the baseline vs current snippet.

alex: repro steps that worked for me locally:
```
git checkout HEAD~5
docker build -t perf-harness .
docker run --rm perf-harness ./bench --model gpt-small --seq 512 --batch 8 --warmup 200 --iter 200 --concurrency 4
```
Measure p99 from the bench output.

priya: I tried toggling kernel selector flags locally — when I set prefer_dense_kernels=false p99 jumps. With it true we're fine. Looks like selector picks a slower fallback kernel for some sequence lengths.

matt: can you confirm which commit introduced that flag change? alex, can you run `git show 7a1b2c3` and paste diff? I think it edits selector.cpp around the heuristics.

alex: git show 7a1b2c3 is indeed a small change in selector.cpp (3 lines) that reorders a branch. It also touched a comment.

sam: starting bisect now. Starting range: good=v1.23.4 (sha 55aabb) bad=HEAD (abcdef1234). I'll run with the above harness and report back.

ci-bot: perf/smoke job queued by sam for commit 7a1b2c3.

sam: quick update — after ~4 steps of bisect the culprit pointed at commit 7a1b2c3. Re-applying that commit locally reproduces the p99 increase; reverting it returns p99 to baseline.

alex: profile snippet when the regression is present (short):
```
-- perf sample breakdown --
select_kernel.cpp:142   47.2%
kv_cache.cpp:88         11.0%
gpu_wait                3.5%
other                   38.3%
```
select_kernel is the largest hotspot.

priya: note: that commit also fixed a memory edge case for long sequences (avoided unbounded kv-cache growth). If we just revert blindly we might reintroduce that.

matt: for immediate mitigation I propose revert commit 7a1b2c3 on master to restore canary latency, then follow up with a patch that retains the mem fix while avoiding the kernel switch for the common seq lengths.

sam: opening PR to revert 7a1b2c3 and run CI smoke: https://internal/pr/3456 (WIP). Bisect logs and bench outputs attached in the PR.

jen: CI smoke after sam's revert branch shows p99 back to baseline on canary. Looks good for rollback path. :tada:

priya: follow-up plan: I'll prototype a selector patch that checks seq-length threshold (e.g., if seq < 64 keep previous kernel ordering) and a unit/perf test that exercises the path. Also add a regression check to the merge checklist.

matt: thanks. Action items: sam -> finish revert PR and coordinate release; priya -> design patch to preserve mem fix; alex -> add perf test harness link & a short runbook for reproducing kernel-selector regressions. I'll put a note in the release postmortem.

sam: revert merged to main and hotfixed to canary. Putting link to revert PR in the incident thread.

jen: marking this as resolved on canary. We'll watch dedicated for a day before promoting.

matt: good work everyone. Follow-up: add a quick perf test to CI that runs the bench for seq 32/128/512 to catch kernel-selection deltas before merges.

priya: I'll own adding the perf matrix and the selector patch.

matt: assigning sam+priya to pair on the selector fix. Thanks all.
